approved: Ozone Protection and Synthetic Greenhouse Gas (Manufacture Levy) Amendment (Carbon Tax Repeal) Bill 2014
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill is part of a package that repeals the carbon tax and prohibits price exploitation on key goods like electricity and gas.
Suppliers of electricity, natural gas, and bulk synthetic greenhouse gases would have to explain to the ACCC how they passed on cost savings from the repeal.
Companies that fail to pass through all savings could face penalties of up to 6,471 penalty units ($1,100,070) and be required to pay 250 per cent of the amount not passed on.
Creates a new prohibition on carbon-specific price exploitation for key goods.
Requires electricity and natural gas retailers and bulk synthetic greenhouse gas importers to give the ACCC a substantiation statement estimating cost savings passed on to customers.
Gives the ACCC monitoring powers to assess the effect of the carbon tax repeal on prices.
Prohibits false or misleading representations about the effect of the carbon tax repeal on prices.
Electricity and natural gas retailers, bulk synthetic greenhouse gas importers, and their customers, as well as the ACCC.

Moved a debate management motion to fast-track passage of the carbon tax repeal bills through the House together, arguing the September 2013 election gave the coalition a clear mandate, and recalled the 2010 pledge that there would be no carbon tax under a government Julia Gillard led.

Moved the second reading of the carbon tax repeal bills, saying Treasury modelling shows households will save an average of $550 a year, that the tax has cost $15 billion over two years, and citing an Independent Competition and Regulatory Commission estimate that electricity prices in the ACT will fall by 11.6 per cent once it is repealed.
